text: Agile is a popular method for managing projects, especially in software development. Instead of planning everything at the start, teams work in short cycles called sprints, which usually last two to four weeks. Each day, they hold a quick standup meeting to share progress and any problems. Before a sprint begins, the team reviews the backlog, a list of tasks to be done, and chooses which ones to work on. These tasks are often written as user stories, simple descriptions of a feature from the user's perspective. Because development is iterative, the team builds and improves the product step by step, gathering feedback after each sprint to make the next cycle better.
